title: Man. Post. Cap. II: four modes of Adam's first sin; Charenton / Walaeus; Calvin quia intra nos
pass_a_gloss: 1. for the act by which he transgressed the law of God, which was the first actual sin. 2. for that same act not taken precisely, but together with the habitual corruption which it brought forth: for these two stand to each other as heating and heat, act and habit, actual change and habitual change. And so both jointly sometimes embrace the same name of Adam's sin, or of the first sin. 3. for the corruption which actual disobedience generated in Adam, and which was his first habitual sin. 4. finally for that same corruption transmitted and propagated into us, which indeed is our sin, because it inheres in us, affects us, and denominates us; yet it is called Adam's sin as of the author, as of the first as it were possessor, as of the fountain whence it flowed down to us. If in this last mode the first sin of Adam is taken, I affirm that it is imputed to all Adam's posterity (one excepted, in whom it had no place, Christ), until they are justified from it through Christ, and I judge their opinion rightly condemned by the Synod of Charenton, who profess that they acknowledge this sin indeed, yet that it is imputed to no one, however unbelieving: for that there are in this age who teach this in published books, the most learned Walaeus testifies and deplores a little before his death in a certain Epistle. Likewise if it is taken in the third mode, I confess it is imputed to us, yet not as it stuck in Adam, but as it passes into us, and, to use Calvin's words, because it is within us: for our hereditary corruption is the same in species with that which once was in Adam; and Adam communicated with us as much his nature as his moral corruption.
pass_b_english: 1. For the act by which he broke God's law—the first actual sin. 2. For that same act not taken by itself, but together with the habitual corruption it produced: the two stand as heating to heat, act to habit, actual change to habitual change. So both together sometimes share the one name 'Adam's sin' or 'the first sin.' 3. For the corruption that actual disobedience bred in Adam—his first habitual sin. 4. For that same corruption as transmitted and propagated into us, which is our sin because it inheres in us, affects us, and names us; yet it is called Adam's as of the author, the first as it were possessor, the fountain from which it flowed to us. If Adam's first sin is taken in this last sense, I say it is imputed to all Adam's posterity (Christ alone excepted, in whom it had no place) until they are justified from it through Christ; and I judge rightly condemned by the Synod of Charenton the opinion of those who profess to acknowledge this sin yet deny that it is imputed to anyone, however unbelieving—for that some in this age teach so in print, the learned Walaeus testified and mourned shortly before his death in a letter. Likewise if it is taken in the third sense, I grant that it is imputed to us—not as it clung in Adam, but as it passes into us, and, in Calvin's words, because it is within us: for our hereditary corruption is the same in kind as that which once was in Adam; and Adam shared with us his nature and his moral corruption alike.
source_text: 1. pro actione qua dei legem est transgressus, quae primum fuit peccatum actuale. 2. pro eadem illa actione non praecise accepta, sed simul cum habituali corruptione quam peperit: habent enim se haec duo velut calefactio et calor, actus et habitus, mutatio actualis et mutatio habitualis. Itaque utrumque conjunctim idem nomen peccati Adami, vel primi peccati nonnunquam complectitur. 3. pro corruptione, quam actualis inobedientia genuit in Adamo, quaeque fuit ejus primum peccatum habituale. 4. denique pro eadem illa corruptione in nos transmissa et propagata, quae nostrum quidem peccatum est, quia nobis inhaeret, nos afficit, et denominat; dicitur tamen peccatum Adami ut authoris, ut primi veluti possessoris, ut fontis unde ad nos defluxit. Si hoc ultimo modo sumatur primum Adami peccatum, aio illud omnibus Adami posteris (uno, in quo locum nullum habuit, Christo excepto) imputari, donec ab eo per Christum justificentur, eorumque sententiam jure damnatam a Synodo Carentonensi arbitror, qui hoc quidem peccatum agnoscere se profitentur, nulli tamen imputari, quantumvis infideli: esse enim hoc saeculo qui id doceant editis libris testatur et deplorat paulo ante obitum suum in quadam Epistola doctissimus Walaeus. Similiter si tertio modo sumatur, fateor nobis imputari, non tamen qua haesit in Adamo, sed qua in nos transit, ac, ut verbis utar Calvini, quia intra nos est: est enim nostra corruptio haereditaria eadem specie cum illa, quae olim fuit in Adamo; ac quam suam naturam, tam suam corruptionem moralem nobiscum Adamus communicavit.
